paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus is the one who gives life, and everything in this passage points at Him. A man lay there for thirty-eight years waiting on a pool, and Jesus made him well with one word (John 5:5, 8-9). Then Jesus says the Son gives life to whom He wishes, and that whoever hears His word and believes the One who sent Him "has crossed over from death to life" (John 5:21, 24). Jesus never had to put that man in the pool, and I'm not sure the man saw that coming either.

Now look at how many witnesses Jesus lines up: John, His works, the Father and the Scriptures (John 5:33-39). The people He was talking to studied those Scriptures hard, and Jesus said those very words testify about Him, yet they refused to come to Him to have life (John 5:39-40). Friend, you can read the whole book and still miss the One it's pointing at. I have flipped through a recipe a hundred times and never once tasted the cookie, so I'm laughing at myself here.

So what do we do with that? We read the Word to meet Jesus, not just to collect facts about Him. He asks the closing question of this passage, "But since you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?" (John 5:47). Come to Him, hear His word and believe, and that's life. That's why I keep my ovens ready, baker.
